messages:
Alex: Bringing up ap-northeast-3 cluster — need a quick, repeatable performance validation runbook focused on p95 latency, throughput baselines, and kernel/driver sanity. I sketched steps below, please review and add checks we missed.

Alex: Runbook (short):
1) kernel/driver checks
   - verify kernel version and NVIDIA driver match matrix
   - modprobe/nvidia errors, dmesg scan for GPU faults
   - check nvidia-container-runtime + container hooks
2) NIC/MTU/RDMA checks
   - iperf3 node pair, mtu, and b/w notes
3) NCCL/allreduce smoke across 4 nodes
4) Serving benchmark
   - synthetic throughput (tokens/sec) and p50/p95 latency
   - end-to-end sample: batching patterns, cold vs warm KV cache
5) Document p50/p95 targets and failing criteria
6) Handoff checklist to SRE + Prod Eng

Priya: +1 on steps. For (1) add: confirm CUDA toolkit vs driver with `nvidia-smi` and `cudaGetDeviceProperties` inside a container. Also check MIG mode if any nodes are partitioned.

Jun: Can we standardize commands? I usually run this sequence: 
```
# on host
uname -a
cat /etc/os-release
modinfo nvidia | grep -E 'version|alias'
journalctl -k -u nvidia-persistenced --no-pager | tail -n 200
dmesg | grep -i -E 'nvrm|nvidia|gpu|pte' | tail -n 200
# sanity
nvidia-smi -q -x | head -n 80
# in container
docker run --gpus all --rm nvidia/cuda:12.1-base nvidia-smi
```
Small snippets let us spot driver mismatches early.

Carlos: I ran the host checks on node-gpu-13 earlier. Quick paste: `Linux node-gpu-13 6.5.0-rc2 ...`, `NVIDIA-SMI 535.86.01 Driver Version: 535.86.01`, no dmesg GPU oops. Attaching short output: 
```
GPU 0: A100-SXM4-80GB
FB Memory Usage: 78%
Utilization: 3%
Compute Processes: none
```
So drivers look OK.

Marta: Networking note — mtus across racks were inconsistent during probe. I ran: 
```
# check MTU
ip link show eth0
# iperf3 between node-gpu-13 and node-gpu-14
iperf3 -c 10.0.2.14 -P 4 -t 30
```
iperf3 reported ~9.1 Gbps on 10G link when MTU=1500, but jumped to 11.8 Gbps with mtu 9000. We should standardize to jumbo frames for bulk NCCL.

Alex: Good catch. Add MTU=9000 as recommended for NCCL to the runbook. Also record pcie link speeds: `lspci -vvv | grep -A20 -i nvidia` and `nvidia-smi topo -m`.

Jun: For NCCL test I use the NCCL tests image: 
```
docker run --gpus all --rm -it nvcr.io/nvidia/nccl-tests:2.14 bash
# inside
mpirun -np 8 -x NCCL_DEBUG=INFO -x NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0 --map-by ppr:1:node ./build/all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 512M -f 2
```
Target: AllReduce bw >= 55 GB/s for 8 GPUs across a single host (A100 SXM) and cross-node ~25-35 GB/s depending on network.

Carlos: Ran NCCL quick run on single node: local all-reduce reported 62 GB/s. Cross-node baseline between gpu-13 and gpu-14: 28 GB/s (with jumbo frames). Without jumbo frames dropped to ~18 GB/s.

Priya: Excellent. For serving synthetic bench, here's a minimal LLM serving harness we use for baselining:
```
# run inside a container that mirrors prod runtime
python bench_runner.py --model redwood/llama-70b --batching [1,4,8] --seq-len 512 --tokens 2000 --concurrency 4 --report p50,p95
```
Targets for this region (initial): p50 < 80ms per token, p95 < 250ms per token at batch=1 with warm KV cache for the short-seq workload. Throughput target: >= 1200 tokens/sec sustained across 8 GPUs (distributed serving).

Marta: I kicked off bench_runner on node-gpu-13 with a small harness. Early numbers: batch=1 p50=68ms, p95=210ms, tokens/sec ~900 on single node (A100-80). Distributed run across 4 nodes gave tokens/sec 3700 (aggregate) but p95 spiked to 420ms occasionally — looks like occasional network stalls.

Alex: Note that distributed serving must tolerate p95 spikes — add a regression alert if p95 increases by >20% relative to baseline during rollout. Also log NIC error counters: `ethtool -S eth0` and `dmesg` for carriers.

Jun: Adding driver/kernel specific checks we must capture to the handoff doc:
- Kernel version string and whether CONFIG_IOMMU is enabled
- Presence of vfio-pci vs nvidia-drm modules (for MIG passthrough)
- `modprobe --verbose nvidia` exit codes
- Verify hugepages settings for some inference stacks

Carlos: build-bot just posted the automated smoke: 
build-bot: "ap-northeast-3-smoke: kernel-check PASS, nvidia-smi OK, NCCL quick: local 62 GB/s, cross-node 28 GB/s (mtu9000)." :white_check_mark:

Priya: Handoff checklist (short):
- Attach full runbook + raw logs (dmesg, nvidia-smi -q xml, iperf3 logs, nccl logs)
- Baseline dashboard link (p50/p95 tokens, tokens/sec)
- Known caveats (MTU requirement, kernel 6.5 recommended, driver pinned to 535.x)
- Rollout gating: if cross-node p95 > baseline*1.2 or NCCL bw < 80% of target, block auto-scaling.

ops-bot: Handoff ticket created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-3210 — assigned to SRE oncall.

Marta: Quick follow-up — small script to collect artifacts (I can add to ops runbook):
```
#!/bin/bash
OUT=/tmp/cluster-baseline-$(date +%s)
mkdir -p $OUT
uname -a > $OUT/uname.txt
nvidia-smi -q -x > $OUT/nvidia-smi.xml
dmesg | tail -n 500 > $OUT/dmesg.txt
iperf3 -c $PEER -J > $OUT/iperf3.json || true
# NCCL logs appended
```
I'll PR that into infra/playbooks after tests run.

Alex: OK let's lock this in. Action items: Carlos finalize node list and repeat runs across 3 node-pairs, Jun produce NCCL test script with env vars, Marta adds artifact collector & MTU enforcement note, Priya drafts gating rules for rollout. I'll do the handoff ticket write-up with links to dashboards. Thanks everyone :rocket: 

Jun: I'll post the NCCL flags and env var doc in the ticket later today.

Carlos: Doing another distributed bench now, will paste final numbers in thread when done.

build-bot: "ap-northeast-3-bench: distributed tokens/sec=3890, p50=72ms, p95=265ms, anomalies=2 (packet drops)"

Carlos: Final note — we saw 2 packet drops on node-gpu-15->gpu-18 link at 03:12 UTC, ops ticket updated. Otherwise numbers look acceptable for initial handoff.

Alex: Great. I'll schedule a brief handoff call with SRE and Prod Eng tomorrow. If anyone finds regression runs where p95 > 300ms please flag immediately.
